correctness.rationale: Chromatic–Tutte duality and finite-difference inversion are explicit; high-girth fixed-argument growth from Bencs–Csikvári proves leading-term dominance. Differentiation shows log-growth derivative strictly increases through its first branch, is above 1/[2(d−1)] between d−1 and d, then below after d, with strict concavity for x≥d. This proves the exact fixed-index sign partition. A standalone rational arithmetic test verifies 7,301 finite parameter cases; it is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The verified 2026 primary theorem proves only a fixed index j=2 failure for d≥4, while the 2021 theorem provides evaluations without this full-index curvature sign classification. The new contribution proves sharp local recovery at j=d−1 and strict positive fixed-index curvature for cubic graphs, while explicitly depending on the older Tutte asymptotic. Search and near-literature comparisons show no known direct implication already stated, subject to unindexed historical priority.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed results may have derived some or all of the same coefficient-curvature frontier from the 2021 Tutte-evaluation theorem.
The 2026 tau paper was revised after initial public appearance; its original stated all-index scope was checked, but future revisions might broaden it.
The related 2026 graph-join paper was reviewed at abstract level, not full text.

value.rationale: A mathematically natural all-fixed-index local phase diagram resolves exactly where the 2026 low-index non-log-concavity mechanism ends, reveals strict local curvature recovery and gives the opposite all-fixed-index behavior in cubic regular graphs. It directly advances understanding of the coefficient-shape question without confusing fixed-index asymptotics with global unimodality.
